name: Carry out periodic mandatory vehicle inspections
summary: Every tractor, truck and trailer over 4,500 kg must pass a periodic inspection to the National Safety Code standard every 12 months, done by a licensed technician at a licensed facility, and must carry the certificate and decal. The planner books each unit before its certificate expires, usually together with its annual C service; a licensed technician inspects and measures the brakes and other systems, repairs defects, and the foreman signs the certificate. The hard parts are getting units back to a licensed shop before expiry, keeping brake measurements and certificates complete for audits, and having enough licensed technicians.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees with twelve company maintenance shops at its hubs and larger terminals, about 1,190 company power units and 4,120 trailers.
baseline.notes: Ontario, Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan and Manitoba units follow the annual periodic inspection; Quebec-plated units are maintained under an SAAQ-recognized preventive maintenance program instead of SAAQ mechanical inspection. Inspections done in the US are not accepted on return.

unit_of_work: one periodic inspection of one tractor, truck or trailer
trigger: A unit's inspection certificate is due to expire within the next one to two months.
end_state: The unit has passed, carries a new certificate and decal, the record is filed for the facility audit and the expiry date is updated.

volume.seasonality: Even through the year, since expiry dates follow each unit's in-service date; new-unit deliveries bunch some expiries.

evidence.note: Every truck, tractor and trailer over 4,500 kg needs an inspection every 12 months; about 5,310 company units in the organisation file divided by 12 gives 443 a month. Owner-operator tractors are inspected by their owners and not counted.

Organisation file role (headcount 8); title, cost and shift from the organisation file, which loads wages by 1.30 for hourly staff and 1.35 for salaried staff. Planners book inspections ahead of expiry and update certificate records.

Transportation management system (LTL and truckload operations, billing, rating)
Email, phone system and contact centre software
Document imaging for bills of lading and delivery receipts
Safety management system (driver files, collisions, roadside inspections)

steps.name: List units with inspections expiring
steps.description: At the start of each month the fleet maintenance system produces a list of tractors, trucks and trailers whose annual inspection certificate expires in the next 30 to 60 days, by home shop.

evidence.note: Monthly report is the author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Plan the inspection with the C service
steps.description: The maintenance planner matches each expiring unit with its next PM so the inspection is done in the same visit as the annual C service, picks a shop that holds the provincial inspection licence for that vehicle type, and books a day close to the expiry date so the new certificate keeps the cycle.

error.defect_description: Booking made past the expiry date or at a shop not licensed for trailers or for air-brake vehicles.

evidence.note: C service normally includes the annual inspection (guide); inspection only at licensed stations (MTO); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request the unit from operations
steps.description: The planner emails the dispatcher or driver manager with the unit, the inspection date and the expiry date, stressing that the unit cannot be dispatched after the certificate expires.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the unit for inspection
steps.description: The dispatcher checks the unit's assignments and agrees a slot. Because an expired unit cannot run, units near expiry get priority, but freight peaks and units away from their home terminal still cause rebooking.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Assign a licensed inspector and bay
steps.description: The foreman assigns the job to a technician who holds a valid inspection licence for the vehicle type and a bay with a pit or hoist, and prints the inspection form or opens the certificate record.

control.basis: Provincial inspection licences: Ontario licensed motor vehicle inspection station and mechanic (HTA Regulation 611); Alberta Vehicle Inspection Regulation (AR 211/2006) facility and technician licences

evidence.note: Inspections by licensed mechanics or technicians at licensed facilities; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Bring the unit to the shop
steps.description: The shunt driver collects the trailer or tractor from the yard, or from the customer site where a trailer was dropped once it is released, and parks it at the shop.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up and lock out
steps.description: The technician moves the unit over the pit or onto the hoist, chocks the wheels, locks out the ignition and drains the air tanks where the procedure requires, so the chassis and brakes can be inspected safely.

control.basis: Shop lockout and vehicle support procedures under provincial occupational health and safety rules

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect to NSC Standard 11 Part B
steps.description: The technician inspects every item in the standard for the vehicle type: brake push-rod stroke, drum and lining thickness, air system and hoses, steering, suspension, frame, coupling devices, lights, tires and wheels, and a visual check of emissions equipment, writing each measurement on the report.

error.defect_description: Item passed that is out of limits, or a measurement not recorded.

control.basis: National Safety Code Standard 11 Part B periodic inspection, adopted by provincial regulation (Ontario HTA Regulation 611, Alberta AR 211/2006)

evidence.note: Standard and recorded brake measurements from the sources; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Do the wheel-off brake inspection
steps.description: When the unit's wheel-off interval is reached, two technicians pull the wheels and drums on each axle, measure drum and lining wear, check seals and hardware, and refit the wheels to torque.

evidence.note: Revised standard limits time between wheel-off brake inspections (12 months for disc brakes, 24 months for a full drum-removed inspection); share and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide pass or repair
steps.description: The technician compares the findings with the reject criteria in the standard and decides whether the unit passes as is, has defects that can be fixed during this visit, or needs a major repair before it can pass.

evidence.note: Pass and repair shares are the author's estimate for a fleet that does regular PMs.

steps.name: Issue parts for repairs
steps.description: The partsperson looks up and issues the brake parts, lamps, hoses or air fittings the technician needs, or orders them if not in stock.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Repair the defects
steps.description: The technician fixes the defects found: adjusts or replaces slack adjusters and brake chambers, replaces lamps and lenses, repairs air leaks, replaces worn hoses or mud flaps.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-inspect repaired items
steps.description: The technician re-inspects and re-measures each repaired item against the reject criteria in the standard and records the after-repair values on the inspection report next to the original finding.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the inspection report
steps.description: The technician completes the inspection report with all measurements, defects and repairs, enters it in the fleet maintenance system, and completes the provincial certificate (the station's numbered certificate in Ontario, the eFacility record in Alberta).

error.defect_description: Measurement or unit number copied wrongly onto the certificate.

evidence.note: Certificates and decals are issued through the provincial schemes; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign the certificate
steps.description: The foreman checks the report for completeness, that brake measurements are recorded and repairs are within limits, and that the certificate shows the right unit and plate, then signs it as the station's authorised signer.

control.basis: Inspection certificate signed by the licensed inspection station or technician (Ontario HTA Regulation 611; Alberta AR 211/2006)

next.condition: item out of limits or missing; back to the technician

evidence.note: Certificate issued by the licensed station; review share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the unit for major repair
steps.description: For a defect too large to fix during the inspection visit (cracked frame member, worn kingpin, failed suspension), the foreman opens a repair work order, tags the unit out of service and sends it to the repair queue; the inspection resumes when the repair is done.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-present the unit after repair
steps.description: When the repair work order is signed off, the foreman puts the unit back on the inspection board for the licensed technician to finish the inspection.

evidence.note: Wait reflects the defect repair process, including parts waits; author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply the decal and file the certificate
steps.description: The technician fixes the inspection decal to the unit and puts a copy of the certificate in the cab document holder; the original is scanned into the vehicle file.

evidence.note: Decal and certificate required; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the inspection record
steps.description: The maintenance planner enters the new inspection date and expiry in the fleet maintenance system so the next expiry list is right, and checks that the scanned certificate is attached to the unit record for the facility audit.

control.basis: Periodic inspection records reviewed in provincial carrier facility audits (NSC Standard 11 Part A, NSC Standard 15)

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the unit
steps.description: The foreman sets the unit status to available in the TMS and phones or emails dispatch that the unit has a new certificate and can be assigned to loads again.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the fleet for expired inspections
steps.description: Each month the compliance specialist compares the active unit list with inspection expiry dates and the scanned certificates, and chases any unit running on an expired certificate or missing a certificate copy.

evidence.note: Units with expired inspections are a facility audit finding in the organisation file; monthly check is the author's estimate. Minutes are per unit.

exceptions.name: Major repair before the unit can pass
exceptions.description: A defect too large to fix in the visit sends the unit to defect repair; the inspection finishes afterwards.

exceptions.name: Unit away from its home shop at expiry
exceptions.description: Dispatch cannot release the unit, or it is on a long run, and the planner rebooks; some units are parked when their certificate expires.

exceptions.name: Wheel-off brake inspection due
exceptions.description: Two technicians pull wheels and drums to measure brake wear, adding about an hour.

exceptions.name: Certificate error
exceptions.description: The foreman finds a missing measurement or wrong unit details and sends the job back.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from expiry list to record verified in the monthly compliance check
benchmarks.population: Company tractors and trailers at a Canadian carrier, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: the list comes out early in the month, the unit is in the shop about a week later, and the record is verified at the next monthly compliance check about ten days after the inspection on average. The unit is off the road for only the shop visit.

benchmarks.population: Ontario and Alberta commercial vehicles over 4,500 kg

evidence.note: An annual inspection is valid for 12 months.

pain_points.description: Units on long runs or held by operations miss their booked slot, so certificates come close to expiry and some units are parked.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes units with expired inspections cannot be dispatched and are a facility audit finding; author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Only licensed technicians can inspect, and the diesel technician shortage limits how many inspections a shop can do.

evidence.note: Licensing requirement and reported technician shortage.

pain_points.description: Brake measurements and certificate details copied by hand are incomplete or wrong, which shows up in audits.

evidence.note: Revised standard requires brake measurements on the report; error rate is the author's estimate.

assumptions: Inspection minutes are counted separately from the C service done in the same visit, which is in the preventive maintenance workflow.
s04 uses the linehaul dispatcher for all operations releases; city dispatchers and truckload driver managers do the same step.
Quebec units under an SAAQ-recognized PEP follow the same steps with the PEP maintenance sheet in place of a provincial certificate, by mechanics who passed the SAAQ PEP examination.
The monthly compliance check (s21) is a batch; its wait adds about nine days to the cycle time but nothing to the unit's time off the road, which is about one day.
The workflow adds equipment availability to dispatch processes as outputs; the organisation file lists only defect repair work orders and certificates for the facility audit.
The NSC Standard 11 text itself could not be opened; requirements are taken from the MTO, Alberta and Trucknews pages cited.

sources.title: Commercial vehicle safety requirements (archived copy of the MTO page, captured 28 August 2021)
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Transportation, via Library and Archives Canada web archive
sources.supports: Annual inspection of trucks, trailers and converter dollies over 4,500 kg by a licensed motor vehicle inspection mechanic at an MTO-licensed inspection station to NSC Standard 11 Part B as modified by Regulation 611; an annual inspection is valid for 12 months and a sticker is applied; daily trip inspection within 24 hours before driving under Regulation 199/07 with a schedule and a report; minor defects reported to the operator as soon as possible; a vehicle with a major defect may not be driven until repaired; the operator must repair defects immediately or before the next dispatch and keep records of repair.

sources.title: Vehicle Inspection Program - Commercial vehicles
sources.supports: All commercial vehicles as defined by the National Safety Code need an annual commercial vehicle inspection (trucks, truck-tractors, semi-trailers and trailers over 4,500 kg registered for extra-provincial operation); inspections are done at private facilities by technicians licensed by Carrier and Vehicle Safety; vehicles must carry a valid inspection certificate and decal under the Vehicle Inspection Regulation (AR 211/2006).

sources.title: Preventative maintenance program
sources.publisher: Societe de l'assurance automobile du Quebec
sources.supports: Owners of heavy vehicles (GVWR 4,500 kg or more) may have a preventive maintenance program recognized by the SAAQ instead of submitting vehicles to mandatory periodic mechanical inspection; owners must follow the maintenance interval schedule and fill out and keep maintenance sheets; mechanics working on vehicles of 7,258 kg or more must have passed a preventive maintenance examination recognized by the SAAQ.

sources.title: You will be tested on this (revised NSC Standard 11 periodic motor vehicle inspection)
sources.supports: Most provinces inspect commercial vehicles of 4,500 kg or more every 12 months; the revised standard requires brake stroke and drum and lining thickness to be recorded on the report and limits the time between wheel-off brake inspections (12 months for disc brakes, 24 months for a full drum-removed inspection); adds a visual emissions-system check; Part A gives maintenance program criteria used in carrier audits and Part B the inspection standard; inspections are done by authorized technicians at authorized facilities; US inspections are recognized only by the home province. The page did not show its publication date; the year given is approximate (the article describes adoption planned for late 2015).

sources.title: Elements of a Successful Preventive Maintenance (PM) Program
sources.supports: PM A service every 5,000 to 10,000 miles on medium and heavy vehicles (safety check, lubrication, key components), B service every 10,000 to 20,000 miles adding oil and filter change and an ECM download with action on trouble codes, C service normally annual and including the annual inspection; trailers on 3-month, 6-month and annual cycles; inspection lanes and yard checks feed the DVIR process; technicians escalate findings to the maintenance supervisor.

sources.title: HDT Fact Book 2022: Trucking fleets focus on preventive maintenance
sources.supports: TMC/FleetNet Q4 2021: 42,459 miles between unscheduled repairs, the highest in two years; top five systems about 67% of roadside repairs; ATRI repair and maintenance cost 14.8 US cents per mile in 2020; shortage of diesel technicians.
